name: The Lachine Sequence: Collapse of a Governing Body
description: One of the earliest serious historical documentaries produced in the newly consolidated Great Lakes corridor, this independent production chronicles the final eighteen months of the Quebec Provincial Authority and its systematic dismantlement through legal attrition, debt acquisition, and infrastructure denial by the precursor entities of what would become HelixCorp and Axiom Consolidated. Drawing on public records that had not yet been sealed, it presents the Lachine Accords of 2171 not as a negotiated transition but as a structured surrender. Shot on flat-screen equipment with minimal production resources, its rough aesthetic has since become a marker of authenticity in documentary circles.
cultural_impact: Established the documentary template that dozens of subsequent independent filmmakers would follow, and its core thesis — that the Sovereignty Transition was a hostile takeover, not a social evolution — remains the foundational argument of every significant anti-corponation historical movement in GLMZ.
story_hooks: The director's original research archive, including documents since sealed or destroyed, was rumored to have been hidden before her death in 2201 — and someone has just started looking for it.
A character working in a HelixCorp legal archive discovers that the Lachine Accords documents referenced in the film have been altered in the official record.
A corponation archivist is tasked with definitively discrediting the film ahead of the 2223 Sovereignty Sesquicentennial, but the research keeps confirming its conclusions.
